thread.title: Close Update: U.S. Stocks Wilt as Washington Ratchets up Trade Tensions, FOMC Turns Hawkish

author: MT Newswires
title: Close Update: U.S. Stocks Wilt as Washington Ratchets up Trade Tensions, FOMC Turns Hawkish

organizations.name: u.s. stocks wilt as washington ratchets up trade tensions

text:
Shutterstock photo Wall Street's major averages were mixed at the close on Wednesday, with stocks weighed by the hawkish tilt of the Federal Open Market Committee and heightened fears of a U.S./China trade war. Led lower by losses in the industrial and energy sectors, the Dow and S&P 500 were underwater while the Nasdaq was kept afloat by gains in tech stocks on the back of strong quarterly results from Apple ( AAPL ).
Wall Street was already defensive at the open as Washington ratcheted up the pressure on Beijing amid signs recent trade talks had again faltered. President Donald Trump warned of 25% tariffs on $200 billion in Chinese imports, provoking China to push back with threats of retaliation.
Labor market data was also a drag on equities as the better-than-expected increase in private payrolls nudged the 10-year yield back to the 3.0% goalpost, rekindling worries about borrowing costs and adding further pressure to stocks.
Data this morning included a slight decline in the final July purchasing managers index (PMI) to 55.3 from the 55.5 flash, and a drop in the corresponding Institute for Supply Management (ISM) index to 58.1 in July from 60.2 in June.
Construction spending was unexpectedly soft in June as a 1.1% decline nearly offset May's 1.3% gain. Homebuilders wobbled on the news, but recovered later in the day to close mostly higher.
The headline event, however, was the FOMC meeting. The outcome was as expected, but statements pertaining to robust economic growth and inflation targets spooked Wall Street. The negative price action was amplified by news Trump was going to announce another round of tariffs against China. After the close, the president directed U.S. trade rep Robert Lighthizer to consider increasing the tariff on $200 billion in Chinese imports, sending stock futures still lower in afterhours trade.
